cleansingStrength.rationale: Strong remains final because the position-2 olefin sulfonate chassis is reinforced by sarcosinate and other secondary surfactants; sulfate-free positioning does not make the non-sulfate chassis mild.
cleansingStrength.counterSignal: Glycerin, shea butter, hyaluronate and cationic polymers buffer the cleanser system but do not erase the strong anionic base.

conditioningLevel.rationale: High conditioning remains plausible because glycerin, glycol distearate, shea butter, hyaluronate and two cationic polymers converge; curl/moisture positioning corroborates the care direction but does not determine the band.
conditioningLevel.counterSignal: Strong olefin/sarcosinate cleansing and no silicone keep confidence moderate rather than high.

weightPotential.rationale: Moderate weight potential remains final because shea butter, hyaluronate and two cationic polymers can deposit, while strong cleansing and no silicone prevent a high-persistence call.
weightPotential.counterSignal: Olefin sulfonate and sarcosinate give strong reset capacity, and the silicone-free claim agrees with no silicone in the INCI.

unresolvedFacts: Same-GTIN dm tail/order delta is preserved and not merged; it is unlikely to move this band because the major surfactant and care routes remain aligned.
weightAssessment.whyThisBand: Butter, film-forming humectant and two cationic polymers can create noticeable but bounded residue.
weightAssessment.whyNotNeighborBand: High would overstate persistence under a strong anionic cleanser system; low would ignore the butter/polymer convergence.

focusPrimary.rationale: General is final under v1.4 because the revealed dominant positioning is curl/moisture, and neither curl nor moisture exists as a v1.4 focus value; repair would overstate a claim not made.
focusPrimary.counterSignal: The formula has a strong moisture/curl care route, but v1.4 cannot encode that directly and the product is not positioned primarily as repair.

focusSecondary.rationale: No secondary focus remains final because the moisture/curl claim and care formula route are not separable into an allowed distinct v1.4 secondary.
focusSecondary.counterSignal: A v1.5 moisture overlay would likely be more expressive, but Lane A v1.4 stays within the frozen enum.

usageRole.rationale: Regular remains final because the directions are standard wet-scalp application and rinse-out, with no treatment or reset cadence trigger.
usageRole.counterSignal: Strong cleansing would matter if reset/oily-root positioning were revealed, but the revealed role is curl/moisture care.

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: Not targeted remains final because the scalp is named only as the application area; the claims target curly hair moisture, not sensitive, itchy or uncomfortable scalp.
scalpComfortTarget.counterSignal: Moisture ingredients can support hair feel but do not establish scalp-comfort targeting.

dandruffSupport.rationale: Not supported is mechanical: the complete INCI contains neither Piroctone Olamine nor Climbazole.
dandruffSupport.counterSignal: Salicylic Acid is present but is not a v1.4 recognized anti-dandruff active by itself.

postUnblindDeltas.reason: Revealed curl/moisture positioning confirms that v1.4 lacks the exact focus bucket; general is retained with higher confidence rather than inventing repair.

unchangedProperties.reason: Sulfate-free wording does not change the strong olefin/sarcosinate formula architecture.
Moisture/curl claims corroborate, but do not change, the formula-derived high conditioning call.
Claims cannot assign weight; butter/polymer deposition plus strong reset remains moderate.
No allowed v1.4 secondary is distinct from the dominant moisture/curl route.
Standard directions do not provide a non-default trigger.
Scalp application wording is not scalp-comfort positioning.
